events.title: FDA Modernization Act 2.0
events.summary: The statutory framework becomes method-neutral and explicitly names cell-based assays, organ chips, microphysiological systems, and computational modeling.
events.why_it_matters: Changes the legal baseline under which non-animal evidence can support drug development.

events.title: Complement-ARIE concept approved
events.summary: The NIH Council of Councils approves the Complement-ARIE concept following ACD recommendations.
events.why_it_matters: Creates the programmatic basis for a large NIH validation, qualification, data, and technology-development effort.

events.title: First organ-on-chip LOI accepted into ISTAND
events.summary: FDA CDER accepts the first organ-on-chip Letter of Intent into ISTAND: a human Liver-Chip proposed to assess drug-induced liver injury risk for certain drug candidates.
events.why_it_matters: Moves an MPS from promising technology into a formal FDA qualification pathway, while remaining distinctly short of qualification.

events.title: Complement-ARIE Validation and Qualification Network launched
events.summary: NIH Common Fund and the Foundation for NIH establish a public-private Validation and Qualification Network to develop and apply reporting, validation, and qualification frameworks for NAMs.
events.why_it_matters: Builds explicit infrastructure intended to convert method development into regulator-ready, reusable evidence packages.

events.title: FDA roadmap begins with monoclonal antibodies
events.summary: FDA publishes its Roadmap to Reducing Animal Testing in Preclinical Safety Studies, beginning with monoclonal antibodies.
events.why_it_matters: Turns statutory possibility into an agency-level implementation program with modality-specific starting points.

events.title: NIH prioritizes human-based research technologies
events.summary: NIH elevates development and use of human-based research technologies as an institutional priority.
events.why_it_matters: Changes funding and research-system incentives independently of FDA qualification pathways.

events.title: ISTAND established as a permanent qualification program
events.summary: FDA transitions ISTAND from pilot status into a permanent program for emerging drug-development tools that do not fit existing qualification pathways.
events.why_it_matters: Institutionalizes a route through which novel technologies can accumulate reusable regulatory credibility.

events.title: $7M Reduction to Practice Challenge launched
events.summary: Complement-ARIE launches a three-phase challenge for integrated human-based NAM platforms, with milestones for fit-for-purpose development, internal validation, reproducibility, and delivery to the VQN.
events.why_it_matters: Creates an explicit pipeline from promising combinatorial NAMs toward practical validation and qualification rather than funding invention alone.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Funding should connect development to qualification and use

events.title: Replacing Animals in Science strategy
events.summary: The UK strategy pairs new funding with dated test-level milestones.
events.why_it_matters: Provides a national roadmap with time-bound implementation targets rather than a general statement of direction.

events.title: Draft guidance streamlines monoclonal-antibody nonclinical safety studies
events.summary: FDA issues draft guidance describing circumstances in which general toxicology studies for monospecific monoclonal antibodies may be unwarranted or shortened, with the stated aim of avoiding unnecessary animal use, particularly non-human primates.
events.why_it_matters: Translates the FDA roadmap into modality-specific regulatory recommendations, but remains draft guidance rather than final implementation.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Policy is beginning to alter modality-specific nonclinical expectations

events.title: AIM-MASH receives formal biomarker qualification
events.summary: AIM-MASH receives formal qualification through FDA's Biomarker Qualification Program rather than ISTAND.
events.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that computational and image-analysis tools can achieve formal qualification through established drug-development-tool pathways.

events.title: EPA recommits to eliminating mammalian testing by 2035
events.summary: EPA formally recommits to the goal of eliminating mammalian testing by 2035 and outlines a strategy centered on identifying usable NAMs, reviewing regulatory flexibility, and encouraging waivers and alternative methods.
events.why_it_matters: Restores a dated agency-wide endpoint against which later implementation and displacement can be measured.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Commitments are becoming time-bounded and operational

events.title: Cross-industry MPS coordination expands through IAMPS and ring trials
events.summary: Cross-industry MPS ring trials and the Industry Alliance for Microphysiological Systems coordinate standards and evidence frameworks.
events.why_it_matters: Industry coordination can turn platform-specific evidence into shared reproducibility and qualification infrastructure.

events.title: FDA issues general draft NAM validation guidance
events.summary: FDA CDER issues draft guidance describing a broad validation framework and scientific principles for NAMs submitted in support of drug development.
events.why_it_matters: Provides general regulatory expectations for establishing credibility across NAM classes instead of addressing only one method or modality. The guidance is draft, not final.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Qualification can become a generalizable regulatory function

events.title: More than $150M in first Complement-ARIE awards
events.summary: NIH announces more than $150 million in the first Complement-ARIE awards to develop, implement, standardize, validate, and scale human-based methods.
events.why_it_matters: Moves Complement-ARIE from program design into funded infrastructure and technology development at substantial scale.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Funding is shifting toward validation and implementation infrastructure

events.title: Year One Progress and accepted-methods resource
events.summary: FDA increases visibility of regulatory use through its Year One progress report and a searchable accepted-methods resource.
events.why_it_matters: Makes prior regulatory use more legible and therefore more reusable as precedent for sponsors and reviewers.

events.title: Draft oncology guidance reduces unnecessary animal testing
events.summary: FDA issues draft guidance for certain cancer drugs describing when nonclinical animal testing may be unnecessary, reduced to a single relevant species, or replaced with evidence-based approaches.
events.why_it_matters: Extends implementation beyond monoclonal antibodies into oncology-specific development decisions. The guidance is draft, not final.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Animal-reduction policy is spreading across drug-development contexts

events.title: EU chemical-safety phase-out roadmap
events.summary: The European Commission publishes a roadmap toward phasing out animal testing for chemical safety across fifteen legislative domains.
events.why_it_matters: Creates a cross-legislative European transition framework whose implementation can be tracked by domain.

events.title: Thirteen NAMs added to accepted lists
events.summary: EPA adds thirteen NAMs to TSCA/FIFRA accepted lists and opens a nomination pathway.
events.why_it_matters: Converts the 2035 commitment into an expanding set of formally usable approaches and a mechanism for continued additions.

events.title: ORIVA formally launches
events.summary: NIH launches the Office of Research Innovation, Validation, and Application to coordinate development, validation, scaling, and regulatory translation of human-based research technologies across NIH.
events.why_it_matters: Creates durable NIH-wide institutional capacity focused on moving human-based methods from innovation toward use.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Institutional capacity is needed for transition from development to application

events.title: Reduction to Practice Phase 1 winners advance
events.summary: Complement-ARIE names Phase 1 winners whose integrated NAM platforms can proceed toward milestone-driven prototype development, internal validation, reproducibility, and potential delivery to the VQN.
events.why_it_matters: Supplies a visible pipeline of near-ready platforms moving toward validation, but does not itself establish validation, qualification, or adoption.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Qualification pipelines are beginning to acquire staged candidates

events.title: ONPRC transition strategy directed
events.summary: The OHSU Board directs a strategic plan to transition ONPRC toward a national center of excellence for NAM development, validation, benchmarking, and implementation; substantially reduce the primate colony; and retain selected NHP research where alternatives are not robustly available.
events.why_it_matters: Signals institutional restructuring of a major primate-research center around NAM development while retaining an explicit boundary for unresolved use cases.

events.title: Animal-model applications must justify use and path to human systems
events.summary: NCI guidance asks animal-model applications to justify animal use and describe a path toward validation in human-based systems.
events.why_it_matters: Changes grant-application expectations so animal use must be defended relative to human-based alternatives and translation plans.

events.title: QSP-based MABEL given a defined early-development role
events.summary: FDA's early-stage development initiative highlights QSP-based MABEL dose selection for first-in-human trials, giving quantitative systems pharmacology a defined role in a decision historically informed by animal toxicology.
events.why_it_matters: Shows computational evidence moving into a concrete development decision rather than remaining a validation exercise.

events.title: Up to $79.3M alternative toxicology contract
events.summary: NIEHS awards an R&D contract valued at up to $79.3 million for computational and alternative toxicological methods across multiple endpoints.
events.why_it_matters: Adds substantial validation and evidence-generation capacity, but should not be treated as proof that a particular human-based method has been adopted.

events.title: 3D airway tissue and digital models enter covered decisions
events.summary: EPA implements 3D human airway tissue plus digital models for certain surfactant respiratory-risk assessments and the GHS mixtures equation for acute oral toxicity of some pesticide formulations, avoiding new animal studies in covered decisions.
events.why_it_matters: Documents decision-level adoption and avoided new animal testing rather than another commitment or validation program.

events.title: Multi-regulator recombinant endotoxin PACMP approved
events.summary: FDA announces completion of an ICMRA collaborative assessment of a multi-product Post-Approval Change Management Protocol using recombinant endotoxin testing as an alternative to horseshoe-crab-derived LAL testing. Participating regulators approved the protocol in June 2026.
events.why_it_matters: Shows coordinated multinational review supporting aligned regulatory action across multiple products and jurisdictions.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Shared evidentiary review can reduce duplicated qualification across jurisdictions
Credibility can become reusable and internationally portable

events.title: Human-based science reviewer recruitment
events.summary: An expression of interest recruits scientists with human-based research expertise for potential peer-review service and a subject-matter-expert directory.
events.why_it_matters: Could improve review-system competence for evaluating human-based methods, but the public posting and durable implementation status still require confirmation.

events.title: Consortium on Advanced Stem Cell-Based Models
events.summary: The consortium brings industry, academic, and regulatory expertise together around drug discovery, safety, precision medicine, validation, benchmarking, reproducibility, and standards.
events.why_it_matters: Provides coordination infrastructure for advanced human model standards and reproducibility, though not itself a qualification decision.
